skill.name: fingerprint-failure-triage
skill.description: Read a liarjs fingerprint report and attribute each failing check to the component that produced it - what the check id measures, whether the signal comes from the launch configuration, the page-modifying layer, the network path or the machine image, and which failures are inherent to headless or datacenter environments. Use when a fingerprint scan came back with a low score, or when a check id such as webdriver, worker-consistency, gpu-triad, native-integrity or tz needs explaining.
skill.summary: Attribute liarjs fingerprint failures to browser launch, page modification, network, or machine sources.
skill.author: liarjsdev

security_audit.summary: Two snippets are genuine npx commands that can download and execute a community package. The remaining backtick, reconnaissance, and URL matches are documentation false positives. The skill also provides a specific technique and iterative workflow that can help reduce browser automation detection.

remediation.issue: The procedure instructs agents to execute liarjs through npx.
remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation, explain that npx may download code, and pin a fully reviewed package version or integrity-verified local installation.

remediation.issue: The debugging-port guidance can help operators avoid the webdriver automation signal.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the bypass detail or restrict it to authorized testing with explicit scope, consent, and anti-abuse boundaries.

content.value_statement: Fingerprint scores often hide which component caused each failure. This skill maps liarjs checks to launch, page, network, or machine sources.
actual_capabilities: Explains what individual liarjs check identifiers measure.
Groups failures by launch, page modification, network, or machine source.
Marks failures expected in headless, proxied, or datacenter environments.
Uses passing checks to distinguish between possible failure sources.
Compares before and after reports to identify changed check statuses.
Separates internal fingerprint coherence from site outcome predictions.
limitations: Requires a liarjs report or named check identifiers as input.
Does not predict whether a specific website will accept a browser.
Does not prescribe configuration changes for every finding.
Network checks may be unavailable when a scan runs offline.

use_cases.title: Triage a low fingerprint score
use_cases.description: Group failed checks by likely source and identify the responsible component.

use_cases.title: Explain one failed check
use_cases.description: Translate a check identifier into its measurement, meaning, and likely owner.

use_cases.title: Compare build results
use_cases.description: Review changed check statuses after one controlled environment update.

prompt_templates.title: Explain one check
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the liarjs check [check id]. State what it measures, the likely source, and whether the result is expected.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a concise explanation of one failure.

prompt_templates.title: Group report failures
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this liarjs report: [report]. Group failures by source, identify owners, and mark failures inherent to the environment.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team needs an owner list from a complete scan.

prompt_templates.title: Compare two scans
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these before and after liarjs results: [before] [after]. Explain changed checks and attribute each change to a component.
prompt_templates.scenario: An engineer changed one environment setting and needs impact analysis.

prompt_templates.title: Build an investigation sequence
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this complete liarjs result: [report]. Prioritize shared root causes, use passing checks as evidence, and separate inherent findings from defects.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user needs a focused investigation plan across several failure groups.

output_examples.input: The report fails worker-consistency while main-thread identity checks pass.
output_examples.output: Source: page-modifying layer. The change reached the main thread but not the separate Web Worker realm. Assign this to the identity modification owner.

output_examples.input: A proxied datacenter run fails tz but passes browser timezone consistency checks.
output_examples.output: Source: network path. The exit IP region differs from the browser timezone. This is often inherent to proxied datacenter environments.

output_examples.input: The new image fails gpu-age, webgpu-empty, and colordepth together.
output_examples.output: Source: machine image. The failures point to old or software rendering, missing WebGPU adapter details, and a virtual display.

best_practices: Provide the full report because passing checks help distinguish possible sources.
Change one environment variable at a time before rescanning.
Describe improved results as removed contradictions, not guaranteed site acceptance.
anti_patterns: Do not investigate only the total score without reviewing check identifiers.
Do not treat several failures with one source as unrelated defects.
Do not assume every headless or datacenter failure requires remediation.

faq.question: What input does this skill need?
faq.answer: Provide a complete liarjs report, two reports for comparison, or one check identifier.

faq.question: Can it explain a single check identifier?
faq.answer: Yes. It can describe the measurement, likely source, and practical meaning for any documented identifier.

faq.question: Does it fix fingerprint failures?
faq.answer: No. It attributes failures and supports investigation, while configuration decisions remain with the browser operator.

faq.question: Does a higher score guarantee website acceptance?
faq.answer: No. Websites may also evaluate IP reputation, account history, and behavior.

faq.question: Why include passing checks?
faq.answer: Passing checks can eliminate competing explanations for a failure and improve source attribution.

faq.question: Can it analyze offline scans?
faq.answer: Yes, but offline scans omit checks that depend on network and edge observations.
